title: Divers Find What May Be the World’s Oldest Shipwreck
paragraphs: Archaeologists believe they have found the oldest known shipwreck in the world, lying in shallow water off Kekova, west of Antalya in Turkey. The team dates it to about 2700–2400 BCE, which makes it roughly 4,500 years old. The previous record holder was a wreck off Dokos in Greece, about 4,200 years old.

Hakan Öniz of Akdeniz University found the site in 2024 after hearing clues from local sailors. The ship’s timbers have disappeared, but its cargo of large storage jars, many with a raised clay band around the middle, is still on a rocky slope. Divers spent about four months freeing the pottery from barnacles. Some jars, or their clay, may come from the Central Jordan Valley.

There are important limits. The research has not yet been peer reviewed, the date is provisional, and tests on the residue inside the jars are still waiting. The contents may have been olive oil, wine or tree resin. The direction of the voyage is unknown, and the ship may have sunk while sheltering from a storm.

questions.q: What was the previous record wreck?
questions.a: One off Dokos in Greece, about 4,200 years old.

questions.q: Where may some of the jars come from?
Why is the date not certain?
questions.a: The research is not peer reviewed and the date is provisional.
